clue.text: Make one joyful sound about another killing

indicators.note: one sound goes about, that is around, the other, so one word wraps the second

parts.note: singing is a joyful sound you make
another joyful sound, the noise of mirth

explanation.surface: Someone cheers over a rival's demise, as if delighting in a murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' has no meaning of its own: it means another joyful sound, so you read it in the light of the phrase before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughtering is the large-scale or brutal killing of people or animals, a direct synonym.

clue.text: In black cover bible is likely to be protected

indicators.note: the holy book sits in the dark cover, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry, and also a dark fur used as a covering
the AV is the Authorized Version, the King James Bible

explanation.surface: A bible bound in black is likely to be kept safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something savable can be saved, rescued or preserved, so it is capable of being protected.

clue.text: Dent finally appearing in a bumper that's loose

indicators.note: a letter turning up in a phrase sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
bumper as an adjective means unusually large, as in a bumper crop

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word before it is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dent shows up in a car bumper that has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a car's bumper, but here bumper is an adjective meaning big.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal or animal at large is free and on the loose, not captured.

clue.text: Axeman has prostitute cut in two in blow

indicators.note: each 'in' puts one piece inside the next

parts.note: a gust is a blow of wind
II is two in Roman numerals

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: An axe murderer splits a prostitute in two with one blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The grisly surface hides rock slang: an axe is an electric guitar, so an axeman plays one. 'Cut in two' works twice: the word is cut short, then placed in the Roman numeral for two.
explanation.definitionFit: In rock slang a guitar is an axe, so an axeman is a guitarist.

clue.text: I run into crowd up in Alpine region

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
the letters go into the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a lot is a group of people, a crowd
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone jogging into a crowd up in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirol, or Tyrol, is the mountainous region of the Alps straddling Austria and northern Italy.

clue.text: Artist cutting up length of stem

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: cutting, as of a remark, is biting or acid
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: An artist cuts a flower's stem to length, as if arranging a still life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like the action of trimming the stem; it is an adjective meaning sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics a radical is the root form of a word, the base from which others grow, as a stem is.

clue.text: Operation to fix something blown out of proportion

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: surgery on the part of the face you blow, when it is too big for the rest
surface reading: an exaggerated matter, a fuss someone has inflated

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown out of proportion' is an idiom for exaggeration; read literally, it is the organ you blow, sized out of proportion to the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose job is informal for rhinoplasty, cosmetic surgery to reshape the nose.

clue.text: All-male hike, excluding absolutely no one

parts.note: all male means every man
to hike prices is to jack them up

explanation.surface: A walking trip for men only, where not a single person is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Every man jack is an idiom for each and every person, without exception.

clue.text: Composer includes girl in second act of Julius Caesar

indicators.note: the second phrase takes in the girl, holding her inside its letters

parts.note: Caesar's boast was 'veni, vidi, vici' (I came, I saw, I conquered); the second of those three acts is 'vidi'
Val, short for Valerie, a stock crossword girl

explanation.surface: A composer's opera about Caesar features a young woman in its second act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' suggests a play's act; here it is one of the three deeds in Caesar's famous Latin line.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi was the Venetian Baroque composer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: Prude is upset as garment slowly rises

indicators.note: something upset is knocked into disorder, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prim person is flustered when a skirt creeps higher.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that rides up gradually works its way higher on the body, a common idiom.

clue.text: Obscure eponym worked for boy on warship

indicators.note: to obscure is to muddle or confuse, so the letters following are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some forgotten name-giver once laboured as a lad aboard a man-of-war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective for the eponym and 'worked' as its verb; in fact the first is the signal and the second is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A powder monkey was a boy who carried gunpowder to the guns on old sailing warships.

clue.text: Girl got out of dress right in front of soldiers

indicators.note: this phrase places what comes before it ahead of what follows, fixing the order of the parts

parts.note: a robe is a long dress or gown
R is the standard abbreviation for right
the TA, the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A young woman slips out of her frock in full view of a troop of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got out of' looks like undressing, but it is a link: the girl is got out of, that is made from, the pieces that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Roberta is a feminine given name, so it serves as an example of a girl.

clue.text: Catch rabbit with trap closer

parts.note: a catch is a fastening, as is a lock
in British slang to rabbit is to chatter at length, and to jaw means the same

explanation.surface: Trapping a rabbit with a snare that snaps shut.
explanation.walkthrough: Trap is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'; the surface makes it a snare for a rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw, a symptom of tetanus, is a spasm that clamps the mouth shut, so it closes the trap.

clue.text: This writer's view is rubbish!

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: this writer's means mine
an eye is a way of seeing, an outlook or view

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses something with a blunt 'In my opinion, it's garbage!'
explanation.definitionFit: 'My eye!' is an old-fashioned exclamation of disbelief, meaning nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Resisting crackers (unlike sugar in tea)

definitions.meaning: surface reading: holding out against biscuits, or against codebreakers
setter's reading: a problem that defies its solvers, and a substance that will not dissolve, as sugar does in tea

explanation.walkthrough: Crackers are solvers of puzzles; the bracket adds the chemistry sense, since sugar dissolves in tea and this word means it would not.
explanation.definitionFit: Insoluble means both impossible to solve and incapable of dissolving in a liquid.

clue.text: Boy in blue votes for Green term

indicators.note: the boy is placed in the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
a lad is a boy
ays, a variant spelling of ayes, are votes in favour

explanation.surface: A young police officer casts his ballot for the Green Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy in blue' suggests a policeman and 'Green' the party; green here means young and inexperienced, and term means a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days, from Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, are one's youth, when one is green in judgment.

clue.text: Swiss town prepared English lunch and tea

indicators.note: a prepared dish has had its ingredients worked over, so these letters are made up afresh

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Swiss resort laid on lunch and afternoon tea in the English style.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuchâtel is a town in western Switzerland, capital of the canton of the same name.

clue.text: Wife's mouth's burying one under superior kiss

indicators.note: to bury something is to cover it over, so one letter is enclosed
in a down clue, what is under something comes after it

parts.note: U, as in 'U and non-U', denotes upper-class or superior usage
X is the kiss at the end of a letter
oral means of the mouth
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A wife's lips take a peck from a husband who considers himself her superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wife's mouth's' looks like one possessive phrase; the first word is the definition and 'mouth's' means 'of the mouth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxorial means relating to a wife, from Latin uxor, so it is the adjective for wife's.

clue.text: Bent journalist under suspicion

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is under something comes after it

parts.note: a hunch is a suspicion or intuition
ED, short for editor

explanation.surface: A corrupt reporter finds himself under suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' suggests corrupt, which fits the journalist; here it means physically stooped.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunched means bent over with the shoulders raised and the back curved, a stooped posture.

clue.text: Fancy putting forward answer that's pertinent

indicators.note: one letter is lifted from its place and set at the front, so it leaves the word it sat in

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
a fancy is a daydream or flight of imagination

explanation.surface: Proposing a clever reply that is right on point.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in DREAM is moved to the front: AD REM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad rem is Latin for 'to the thing', used of a remark that is relevant to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Idiot upset delicate old empire

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: in a down clue, set upside down means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: airy means light and delicate

explanation.surface: A fool knocks over a fragile antique from an ancient kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was an ancient Mesopotamian empire centred on the upper Tigris, so it is an example of an old empire.

clue.text: Race awkwardly with big skeletal frame

indicators.note: something done awkwardly is clumsy and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a large bony build runs clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: The rib cage is the bony framework of ribs enclosing the chest, part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Measures a stallion, perhaps, by its head

parts.note: taken as written
a mount is a horse for riding, of which a stallion is an example

indicators.note: the head of something is its top or start, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: 'its' points back to the stallion, whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Gauging a horse's height using its head, like a vet sizing up a stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the stallion as one example of a mount; 'its head' then reuses the stallion for a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amounts, as a plural noun, are quantities, which is what measures are.

clue.text: Hindu teacher whirled in front of one

indicators.note: what comes earlier is placed ahead of what follows

parts.note: a head that swam was whirling or reeling
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A spiritual guide spins round in front of a disciple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whirled' suggests a dervish's spin, apt for a holy man; it is the past tense of swim in the sense of a head reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or ascetic, used as a title of respect.

clue.text: Row about stub put out in container

indicators.note: one word goes about, that is around, the other

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or disordered, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An argument over a cigarette end that was stubbed out in a receptacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like stubbing out a cigarette, but it scrambles the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustbin is the British word for a rubbish bin, a household receptacle for waste.

clue.text: Dagger hung in odd positions before a god

indicators.note: what comes earlier is placed ahead of what follows

parts.note: a kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade

indicators.note: only the first, third and other odd-numbered letters are kept

parts.note: the first and third letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dagger is hung up in a temple before the statue of a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Krishna is a major Hindu deity, an avatar of Vishnu, so he is an example of a god.

clue.text: Damage incurred due to being carried up

definitions.meaning: surface reading: harm suffered, as if something were broken in transit; but 'damage' is also slang for a bill, as in 'what's the damage?'
setter's reading: the charge you pay for being borne aloft, that is flown

explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' suggests breakage, but in British slang it means the cost; being carried up is a fanciful way to say flying.
explanation.definitionFit: An air fare is the price of a ticket for travelling by plane, the cost of being flown.

clue.text: A fellow Democrat in Budget retaining cents for Treasury

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a lad is a fellow, a young man
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
taken as written
to budget is to economise, to save
C is the abbreviation for cents

explanation.surface: A Democrat politician keeps a few cents back in the Budget for the Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasury' and 'Budget' paint a picture of government finance; the definition is a different kind of treasury, and 'in' is simply the word IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aladdin's cave, from the Arabian Nights tale, is the stock phrase for a place full of riches, a treasure house.
